title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector assistance to support returned IDPs in Berhale and Kunneba woredas, Zone 2, Afar Region

description.narrative: ltpgtAccording to the GOAL Ethiopia MIRA assessment conducted in September 2023 (attached to this proposal), the humanitarian situation in Berhale and Kuneba woredas in zone 2 (Afar region) continued to deteriorate after the conflict. There are currently thousands of people suffering from the dire aftermath and consequences of war and who are in desperate conditions, looking for an inclusive and urgent escalation of integrated multi-sector humanitarian assistance. Agriculture, health services, nutrition, WASH, education, protection, and mental and psychosocial support are the priority humanitarian needs of the returned IDPs in Berhale and Kuneba woredas, Zone 2, Afar Region.ltbrgtThe needs assessment highlights the critical situation that returned IDPs in Berhale and Kuneba woredas are facing: most of the basic infrastructures including schools, health facilities, and water supply infrastructures were looted and damaged during the conflict, and all the IDPs who are gradually returning to their homes have no or limited access to basic health care and sanitation services, the local government has limited capacity and resources to rehabilitate the infrastructures and resume the services, the schools are still not functional, while the more vulnerable groups (especially children and women) are dealing with serious mental and psychological trauma caused from the conflict.ltbrgtIn this context GOAL Ethiopia (Lead) in partnership with MCMDO (local NGO as Sub-grantee) have designed this intervention with the aim to support IDPs returning to Berhale and Kunneba woredas in zone 2, where both organizations have existing presence, strong knowledge of the situation on the ground, and established relationship with local authorities: these are key factors that will enable the consortium to have impactful multi-sectoral implementation and maximize the results while providing Agriculture, Health, Nutrition, WASH and Education services, with significant cash component and meaningful protection mainstreaming considering significant cross-cutting elements.ltbrgtThrough this 12-months project, GOAL and MCMDO will assist the returnees during the recovery process, support the communities to re-establish their economic and social well-being, and contribute to create a conducive and inclusive environment, by providing life-saving interventions (to reduce nutrition caseloads and improve health conditions) and also integrating some recovery and resilience elements as durable solutions for the sustainability of the intervention (for instance, agriculture inputs, capacity building and cash injections to strengthen the local markets). ltbrgtThrough this project, GOAL and MCMDO expect to reach a total of 133,093 beneficiaries in the two target woredas (Berhale and Kunneba), with a total budget of $ 2,200,000, which has been allocated based on sectoral needs on the ground.ltbrgtThe project is clearly linked to the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), which includes alignment with HRP strategic objectives and relevant cluster objectives and has been designed with field-level MIRA assessment and taking into consideration the security situation, access, market functionality, fluctuations in market price, and others on-going interventions in the target locations, to avoid duplication of effort and resources. ltbrgtThe selection of the prioritized sectors has been done in consultation with the relevant Clusters at national and regional level and based on the MIRA Assessment findings, taking into considerations also the local stakeholders, who have been consulted during proposal development and have endorsed the proposed activities. This project also considers a meaningful inclusion for cross-cutting issues (like, AAP, gender, and disability inclusion) and protection mainstreaming-related activities are reflected in the log frame. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgt
